overview.headline: Using radioactive decay clocks to determine geologic age and history

keyPoints.point: Geologists reconstruct the sequence of events that shaped the Earth's surface from petrology, stratigraphy and paleontology.
keyPoints.quote: today geologists reconstruct the sequence of events that has shaped the Earth's surface.

keyPoints.point: Geologic history is divided into Eras and Periods based on general character of life and major crustal disturbances.
keyPoints.quote: dividing the Earth's history into Eras -- broad spans based on the general character of life

keyPoints.point: Radioactive decay is a spontaneous process where a parent isotope loses particles to form a new element isotope.
keyPoints.quote: Radioactive decay is a spontaneous process in which an isotope (the parent) loses particles from its nucleus to form an isotope of a new element

keyPoints.point: The age equation relates radioactive decay to geologic time using decay constant and daughter to parent ratio.
keyPoints.quote: The mathematical expression that relates radioactive decay to geologic time is called the age equation

keyTerms.gloss: study of rock origins and rock types from investigations of formation
keyTerms.quote: studies on the origins of the various kinds of rocks (petrology), coupled with studies of rock layering (stratigraphy)

keyTerms.gloss: atoms of same element with different atomic weights due to neutron variation
keyTerms.quote: Atoms of the same element with differing atomic weights are called isotopes.

keyTerms.gloss: time required for half of radioactive isotope atoms to decay
keyTerms.quote: The rate of decay is conveniently expressed in terms of an isotope's half-life, or the time it takes for one-half

keyTerms.gloss: constant rate of decay used in age equation to relate half-life and age
keyTerms.quote: delta is the appropriate decay constant.

keyTerms.gloss: broad history of Earth divided into Eras and Periods from geologic record
keyTerms.quote: Geologists have done the same thing to geologic time by dividing the Earth's history into Eras
